4_structural_height_architecture.controlling_member: the deepest BOUND beam band whose footprint enters the column outline; an UNBOUND framing band is admitted only through its upper bound (deepest scheduled section with that drawn breadth): if the bound maximum already reaches it the depth is proved, otherwise BLOCKED_UPPER_MEMBER_UNBOUND; no framing band -> SLAB_SOFFIT with the printed slab thickness of the region
4_structural_height_architecture.interval: structural storey interval = difference of the printed FFLs (4.50 / 4.20 / 4.20), stated as STRUCTURAL_INTERVAL_FROM_FFL_EQUAL_BUILDUP (valid only when the build-ups above and below are equal); a printed structural level would outrank it; context only, never a column height by itself
4_structural_height_architecture.neck: COLUMN_NECK_VOLUME = BLOCKED_HEIGHT: the source gives the footing H but no footing-top / founding level and no ground-beam top; +1.00 FFL is corroboration only
4_structural_height_architecture.lower_support_GF: ground-beam / ground-slab top is not levelled in the structural source; the GF column height is computed with the same interval rule and carries LOWER_SUPPORT_LEVEL_ASSUMED_AT_FLOOR_STRUCTURAL_TOP

physical_model.SLAB: net plate area (inside the slab perimeter, voids / stair / lift openings removed) x printed thickness t, continuous over beams and columns
physical_model.DOWNSTAND_BEAM: CLEAR_FACE_TO_FACE length x B x (D - t)
physical_model.BEAM_COLUMN_JOINT: column plan area x (D_ctrl - t), so a column measured to the controlling soffit and a beam measured face to face leave no gap

5_beam_slab_double_count.invariant: physical total = slab + downstands + joints + columns; every cubic metre is owned by exactly one component (tested on synthetic grids)

12_generic_beam_binding.engine: BEAM_BINDING_V2 (new engine/source/beam_binding.py); structural_schedule.beam_bands stays unchanged (frozen A3 behaviour, still used for straps)
positive_constraints: band = two parallel element lines (any orientation, collinear pieces merged) whose separation equals the scheduled breadth of the TAG'S OWN TYPE (authoring tolerance, then the 5 % width-deviation policy)
orientation: band axis parallel to the tag baseline (rotation read from the source entity) within 1 deg
span: the tag centre projects inside the band's common span
adjacency: the tag box lies inside the band or its near edge is within ONE TEXT HEIGHT of the band edge, with no other element line between tag and band
unique survivor: exactly one band passes all of the above
12_generic_beam_binding.outcomes: BOUND / NO_BAND / AMBIGUOUS_BAND / CURVED_BAND_NOT_SUPPORTED / SECTION_NOT_SCHEDULED - 0 or 2+ survivors BLOCK; never nearest-text
12_generic_beam_binding.robustness: the result is recomputed at 0.5x / 1.5x the adjacency gap and published as a sensitivity record; a tag whose binding changes is not bound
12_generic_beam_binding.lengths: PLAN_DRAWN_EXTENT (common span of the pair), SUPPORT_CENTRELINE_LENGTH (between the centres of the supports the band ends in), CLEAR_FACE_TO_FACE_LENGTH (between support faces), SCHEDULE_SPAN_LENGTH (continuous beams: sum of printed spans) - stored separately
12_generic_beam_binding.namespace: simple (B*), continuous (CB*) and strap (SB*) libraries are looked up only in their own namespace; a B1 lookup can never return CB1 and no normalisation strips a letter

answers.13_slab_outlines_source_only: per slab sheet: polygonise the element lines (beam band edges + column outlines); the slab perimeter is the outer boundary of the union of bounded faces; VOID labels and S-OPENING crosses / outlines define openings (stair / lift / double-height); a perimeter that does not close -> SLAB_OUTLINE_NOT_ESTABLISHED (BLOCK); thickness from the printed 'T / nn' tag of the region (several printed thicknesses on one sheet without a region boundary -> thickness per region or BLOCK); never fitted to any target area
answers.14_stair_concrete_source_only: STAIR_CONCRETE_V1 (new engine/source/stair_concrete.py): waist (sloping length x width x waist) + wedges (0.5 x riser x tread x width x n) + landings (area x thickness) + stair beams separately; the Alsenan source has tread 300 and flight widths but no waist thickness and no riser height -> volume BLOCKED_INPUT_MISSING (WAIST_THICKNESS, RISER_HEIGHT); never steps x 0.30 x 0.15

16_disagreements_with_chatgpt_architectu: Column to the beam soffit + beam clear face to face leaves the beam-column joint in neither item: B2A adds an explicit BEAM_COLUMN_JOINT component so the physical total neither double counts nor omits.

'4.50 - 0.40 = 4.10' treats the FFL difference as the structural interval; that holds only when the floor build-ups above and below are equal. B2A labels the interval STRUCTURAL_INTERVAL_FROM_FFL_EQUAL_BUILDUP and lets a printed structural level outrank it.

Paint and wall-tile heights run from the FINISHED floor, so they need the floor build-up above as well as the soffit; the 150 mm ceiling allowance alone does not make them computable. They stay blocked on the build-up (owner action), while blockwork and plaster (slab top to soffit) do not need it.
'Inner arc' must be defined geometrically (smallest radius) and kept apart from 'room side'; for a curve bulging into a room the room-side face is the larger radius.

The Reception region can be evidenced from the STRUCTURAL slab opening (VOID) projected through the column registration rather than drawn as a free semantic polygon; without that evidence a zone inside an open site would be an invented boundary.

The salon height cannot be 'source-proved' from CB1 alone: CB1 gives the structural soffit (interval - 0.75 - build-up above), an UPPER BOUND for the aluminium head; the head itself (ceiling / fascia below the soffit) is not in the source, so 3.65 stays OWNER_DERIVED with a source-consistency check.
